literal: Hunton County.
idiomatic: Hunton County.

literal: He Prefecture, Dehua Army.
idiomatic: He Prefecture (Dehua Army).

literal: An Arms Workshop was established.
idiomatic: An Arms Workshop was installed.

literal: Xiang Prefecture, Ruisheng Army, military commissioner.
idiomatic: Xiang Prefecture (Ruisheng Army), military commissioner.

literal: Xingzong established it with Tieli households.
idiomatic: Xingzong founded it with Tieli households.

literal: Military affairs subordinate to the Huanglong Prefecture Deployment Office.
idiomatic: Military affairs under Huanglong Prefecture Deployment Office.

literal: Governing one county:
idiomatic: One county:

literal: Huaide County.
idiomatic: Huaide County.

literal: Collation Notes
idiomatic: Collation Notes

literal: 1 From Eastern Capital Liaoyang Prefecture through styled Central Capital Xiande Prefecture: "originally Chaoxian territory"—according to Shiji 115 Chaoxian Traditions and Hanshu 28b Geographic Treatise, it should read "originally Yan state territory."
idiomatic: First note: from Eastern Capital Liaoyang Prefecture through "Central Capital Xiande Prefecture," the phrase "originally Chaoxian territory" should, per Shiji 115 and Hanshu 28b, read "originally Yan state territory."

literal: This section wrongly takes Liaoyang for Pyongyang.
idiomatic: This section wrongly identifies Liaoyang with Pyongyang.

literal: Moreover, according to New Tang History 219 Bohai Traditions, Hohan Prefecture was Shangjing Longquan Prefecture—not Pyongyang, and not Liaoyang.
idiomatic: Per New Tang History 219 Bohai Traditions, Hohan Prefecture was Shangjing Longquan Prefecture, not Pyongyang or Liaoyang.

literal: 2 From Taizu founding the state and attacking Bohai through seizing Hohan city to Shence year 4 repairing Liaoyang old walls and building Dongping Commandery as defense prefecture: repairing Liaoyang and building Dongping come first; attacking Bohai and seizing Hohan come after—the narrative order is inverted.
idiomatic: Second note: repairing Liaoyang and founding Dongping precede the Bohai campaign and seizure of Hohan—the sequence is inverted.

literal: It is suspected that "formerly" two characters were lost before Shence year 4.
idiomatic: Likely "formerly" was lost before Shence year 4.

literal: 3 City named Tianfu: according to the Annals, Tianxian year 1 second month changed Hohan city to Tianfu.
idiomatic: Third note: "city named Tianfu"—the Annals place the Hohan-to-Tianfu rename in Tianxian year 1, month 2.

literal: It was not when Dongping was raised to Nanjing that Dongping was called Tianfu.
idiomatic: Tianfu was not the name given when Dongping became Nanjing.

literal: 4 Governing eighty-seven prefectures, fu, armies, and cities: the figure "eighty-seven" does not match the list of prefectures, fu, armies, and cities below.
idiomatic: Fourth note: "eighty-seven" prefectures, fu, armies, and cities does not match the list below.

literal: 5 "Originally Han Loufang County land": Loufang—in Hanshu Geographic Treatise and Hou Hanshu Commanderies and States both write Loufang, belonging to Lelang Commandery.
idiomatic: Fifth note: "Loufang County"—Hanshu and Hou Hanshu both have Loufang in Lelang Commandery.

literal: 6 "Shengzong returned from campaigning Goryeo": the original erroneously read "Silla"; corrected per Annals Tonghe year 3 seventh month and year 10 first month.
idiomatic: Sixth note: "Goryeo" was written "Silla" in the original; corrected from Annals Tonghe 3.7 and 10.1.

literal: 7 "At the end of Tonghe Goryeo surrendered"—the six characters "at the end of Tonghe, Goryeo surrendered" were wrongly placed after "Kaitai year 3 took its Bao and Ding two prefectures," reversing chronology; now corrected.
idiomatic: Seventh note: "at Tonghe's end Goryeo surrendered" was misplaced after the Kaitai seizure of Bao and Ding—now reordered.

literal: 8 Heduan: Daoguang Hall edition Commentary cites Yongle Encyclopedia as Herui.
idiomatic: Eighth note: Heduan—Daoguang Commentary cites Yongle Encyclopedia's Herui.

literal: 9 "Bohai established the prefecture"—the four characters "Bohai established the prefecture" were originally missing; Daoguang Hall edition added them per Tongkao.
idiomatic: Ninth note: "Bohai established the prefecture" was missing; Daoguang edition restored it from Tongkao.

literal: The present text follows that.
idiomatic: The present text follows that addition.

literal: 10 Qi River: according to Zhao Wanli's collated Yuan Comprehensive Gazetteer
idiomatic: Tenth note: Qi River—per Zhao Wanli's collated Yuan Comprehensive Gazetteer

literal: Opening angle bracket in the citation title.
idiomatic: Opening bracket before the abbreviated gazetteer title.

literal: (hereafter called Collated Yuan Comprehensive Gazetteer); closing bracket.
idiomatic: The text continues as the Collated Yuan Comprehensive Gazetteer, then closes the citation bracket.

literal: Volume 2 has Water.
idiomatic: Volume 2 lists Water.

literal: The character "Qi" is wrong.
idiomatic: The character Qi is erroneous.

literal: 11 "Originally Han Dongnai County land": Daoguang Hall edition Commentary says Han had no Dongnai County; it may be a dropped-graph error for Hou Hanshu Commanderies and States' "Dong" and "Buer."
idiomatic: Eleventh note: Dongnai County—Daoguang Commentary argues Han lacked Dongnai; likely a garble of Hou Hanshu's Dong and Buer counties.

literal: Suoyin suspects it is Tang's tributary Daina Prefecture.
idiomatic: Suoyin suggests Tang's tributary Daina Prefecture.

literal: 12 Suibin County "originally Bohai Suibin Prefecture land": Suoyin: "Since it says Suibin Prefecture households were moved to establish it, it is not the old territory."
idiomatic: Twelfth note: Suoyin observes that relocating Suibin Prefecture households means it is not the original territory.

literal: 13 Qian Prefecture "Shengzong Tonghe year 3 established": according to the Annals, Qianzhou was established in Qianheng year 4 eleventh month.
idiomatic: Thirteenth note: Qian Prefecture's Tonghe year 3—Annals place it in Qianheng year 4, month 11.

literal: 14 Xuan Prefecture: "Xuan" should be Yi.
idiomatic: Fourteenth note: Xuan should read Yi.

literal: This is Zhongjing Circuit's Yi Prefecture.
idiomatic: This is Yi Prefecture of Zhongjing Circuit.

literal: Its county Kaiyi matches Jin History Geographic Treatise; this book's Zhongjing Circuit Yi Prefecture entry writes Wenyi.
idiomatic: Subordinate Kaiyi County matches Jin History; this book's Zhongjing Yi entry reads Wenyi.

literal: 15 "Han Gongsun Du held it"—by context "late" is missing after Han.
idiomatic: Fifteenth note: "Han Gongsun Du held it"—context requires "late Han."

literal: 16 "Originally Bohai Yuancheng County land": Yuancheng—in the Chong Prefecture entry above appears as Lücheng.
idiomatic: Sixteenth note: Yuancheng appears as Lücheng in the Chong Prefecture entry above.

literal: 17 "Bohai built Shen Prefecture; nine former counties all abolished"—Daoguang Hall edition Commentary: "According to the Yuan Comprehensive Gazetteer, Bohai built Dingli Prefecture, superintending Shen and Ding two prefectures, governing Dingli, Pingqiu, Yancheng, Meimei, Anyi, Shenshui, Anding, Baoshan, and Nengli nine counties—all abolished."
idiomatic: Seventeenth note: Daoguang Commentary cites Yuan Comprehensive Gazetteer—Bohai's Dingli Prefecture oversaw nine counties, all abolished.

literal: 18 "At first subordinate to Yongxing Palace"—the character "palace" was originally missing, restored from Barracks and Guards Treatise, upper.
idiomatic: Eighteenth note: "Yongxing Palace" lacked palace, restored from Barracks and Guards Treatise, upper.

literal: 19 "Yi, Meng, Tuo, Hei, Bei five prefectures": Bei—in New Tang History 219 Bohai Traditions appears as Bi.
idiomatic: Nineteenth note: Bei prefecture appears as Bi in New Tang History 219.

literal: 20 Qi Prefecture: Qi was originally written "chess" Qi; corrected per Barracks and Guards Treatise, upper, and Jin History Geographic Treatise.
idiomatic: Twentieth note: Qi was written with the "chess" graph; corrected from Barracks and Guards and Jin History.

literal: 21 "Shengzong changed to the present name through raising to military commissioner": Shengzong came after Jingzong's Baoning.
idiomatic: Twenty-first note: Shengzong's rename followed Jingzong's Baoning era.

literal: Jingzong Baoning year 7 had already added households and raised it to military commissioner; only under Shengzong was it renamed Tong Prefecture.
idiomatic: Baoning year 7 already added households and a military commission; Shengzong then renamed it Tong Prefecture.

literal: 22 Qiangshuai County: Jin History Geographic Treatise writes Qiangshi County.
idiomatic: Twenty-second note: Qiangshuai County is Qiangshi in Jin History.

literal: 23 "Xie Prefecture superintending Xie two prefectures": according to New Tang History 219 Bohai Traditions, Xie Prefecture governed Xie and Gao two prefectures.
idiomatic: Twenty-third note: Bohai's Xie Prefecture governed Xie and Gao, per New Tang History 219.

literal: 24 Haoli Grand Guardian Fort: Hao—in the Annals Kaitai year 8 tenth month appears as Hao (waste).
idiomatic: Twenty-fourth note: Haoli appears as Hao in Annals Kaitai 8.10.

literal: 25 Xin Prefecture "Zhangsheng Army lower military commissioner": according to Officials Treatise 4 it is Xin Prefecture Zhangsheng Army military commissioner—the same.
idiomatic: Twenty-fifth note: Officials Treatise 4 agrees on Xin Prefecture Zhangsheng Army military commissioner.

literal: Juan 91 Yelü Pulidu Traditions—in Taiping times he was repeatedly promoted to Zhangsheng Army military commissioner; Annals Da'an year 8 has Zhangsheng Army military commissioner Yelü Nieli.
idiomatic: Juan 91 Yelü Pulidu rose to Zhangsheng Army commissioner in Taiping; Da'an year 8 names Yelü Nieli.

literal: Below, Ying Prefecture shares the army title with Xin Prefecture but is a cishi prefecture, not a circuit command.
idiomatic: Ying Prefecture shares Xin's army title but is a cishi prefecture, not a circuit seat.

literal: Officials Treatise 4 lists Ying Prefecture among cishi prefectures.
idiomatic: Officials Treatise 4 classifies Ying among cishi prefectures.

literal: Moreover, Princes Table and Juan 82 Xiao Yang'a Traditions have Zhangxin Army military commissioner; Jin History Geographic Treatise writes Xin Prefecture Zhangxin Army.
idiomatic: Princes Table and Xiao Yang'a also mention Zhangxin Army; Jin History has Zhangxin at Xin Prefecture.

literal: 26 "Placed cishi between Yazi and Hunton two rivers":—according to the Annals Taiping year 4 second month: "An edict changed Yazi River to Hunton River," but afterward the name Yazi River was still used; Juan 98 Yelü Yan Traditions: "His father Zhongxi—Qingning year 4 walled between Yazi and Hunton two waters."
idiomatic: Twenty-sixth note: Annals Taiping 4.2 renamed Yazi River Hunton River, yet Yazi River remained in use; Yelü Yan records Zhongxi walling between the two waters in Qingning 4.

literal: 27 "Huanglong Prefecture Deployment Office": Office—the original erroneously read "affairs"; corrected per context, Military Treatise middle, Barracks and Guards lower, and Officials Treatise 2.
idiomatic: Twenty-seventh note: "Deployment Office" was written "affairs"; corrected from context and parallel treatises.

literal: According to context and Military Treatise middle, Barracks and Guards lower, and Officials Treatise 2 corrected.
idiomatic: Corrected from Military Treatise, Barracks and Guards, and Officials Treatise 2.

literal: 28 Anding Prefecture: according to the Annals Tianxian year 1 third month it was Anbian Prefecture.
idiomatic: Twenty-eighth note: Anding Prefecture was Anbian in Annals Tianxian 1.3.

literal: 29 Fu Prefecture Huaide Army military commissioner: according to Jin History Geographic Treatise: "Fu Prefecture, lower, cishi; Liao Huaiyuan Army military commissioner."
idiomatic: Twenty-ninth note: Jin History lists Fu as cishi with Liao Huaiyuan Army military commissioner.

literal: 30 An Prefecture cishi: according to the Annals Tonghe year 28 eleventh month, Ma Baoyou once was An Prefecture regional training commissioner; Juan 94 Yelü Helu Saogu Traditions, early Qingning added An Prefecture regional training commissioner; Officials Treatise 4 also writes regional training.
idiomatic: Thirtieth note: Annals Tonghe 28.11 names Ma Baoyou An regional training commissioner; Yelü Helu Saogu and Officials Treatise 4 agree.

literal: Only State Chronicles 22 lists An among cishi prefectures.
idiomatic: Only State Chronicles 22 lists An as a cishi prefecture.

literal: Perhaps at first it was cishi and later raised to regional training.
idiomatic: Perhaps it began as cishi and was later raised to regional training.

literal: Juan 105 Xiao Wen Traditions: "Father Zhishan, An Prefecture defense commissioner."
idiomatic: Juan 105 Xiao Wen Traditions: "Father Zhishan was An Prefecture defense commissioner."

literal: Civil office in the Dakang and Shouchang period.
idiomatic: He held civil office during Dakang and Shouchang.
